A 39-year-old Nigerian woman with history of sickle cell disease presented to our hospital

attribution_limitations: The abstract places the swelling on the back ("vague back swelling for many years"), the case text places the chief complaint on the left flank ("increased swelling on her left flank for the past 2 years") and the examination describes a fluctuant area of the back; the CT mentions the left lower back/flank subcutaneous tissue. The source does not state that these are the same lesion.

The history gives the swelling size as approximately 10 cm on presentation, while the examination reports a 10 cm × 16 cm fluctuant area of the back; the source does not say these measure the same thing.

The cultures that revealed Mycobacterium tuberculosis are described only as "from drained abscess". The case describes an earlier ultrasound guided drainage and a later paraspinal drainage; the source does not say which drainage supplied the specimen.
The ultrasound guided drainage is described as attempted, with only a small amount of thick, viscous fluid collected.

The regimen at the last clinic visit lists isoniazid, rifampin and pyridoxine only. Pyrazinamide and ethambutol are not named at that visit, and the source does not state when isoniazid was restarted after all medications were stopped.

Right upper quadrant pain and elevated transaminases are reported at TB clinic follow-up, after the anti-TB regimen was started, and the medications were then stopped. The source does not name a cause.

The Figure 1 caption describes an "expansile mass extending into epidural space" while the case text describes an "expansile abscess within substance of the disk extending into ventral epidural space".

The introduction calls the case a cold abscess as the only manifestation of tuberculosis, while the case also documents L4-L5 diskitis/osteomyelitis, cervical lymph nodes, icteric sclera and later right upper quadrant pain with elevated transaminases without stating their cause.

The abstract states that initial studies and cultures were negative for Mycobacterium tuberculosis without naming them; the case text separately reports negative Gram and acid-fast stains of the drained fluid and sterile blood cultures.

The patient and neurosurgeons are described as initially reluctant to perform the surgical drainage; the source does not say the procedure was declined or refused, and a later paraspinal drainage is reported.
The Gram stain and acid-fast staining sentence does not name the specimen; it follows the fluid analysis sentences of the ultrasound guided drainage paragraph.
